title: Model soups: averaging weights of multiple fine-tuned models improves accuracy without increasing inference time
relevance: Averaging the WEIGHTS of several models fine-tuned under different hyperparameter settings improves both accuracy and out-of-distribution robustness, at NO extra inference or memory cost - which matters enormously for us, since our full-city inference already OOM'd at batch 160 on an A100 and a true ensemble over 18 citywide rasters is unaffordable. This is ensemble-grade robustness at single-model inference expense, and it composes with the tuning sweep Q17 already demands: the runs from a hyperparameter search become the soup ingredients rather than being discarded. Note the tension with agreement-on-the-line (ID 153), which NEEDS several distinct models - measure agreement first, then soup for deployment.

title: Robust fine-tuning of zero-shot models
relevance: WiSE-FT: interpolate between the PRETRAINED and the FINE-TUNED weights, giving an explicit dial between base-model robustness and target-task accuracy. Our per-year models are all fine-tuned from sem_best_2020.pt, so this applies with no retraining at all - it is weight arithmetic over checkpoints we already have, and every interpolate can be scored with the existing QC scripts. It is a principled control on how far a coarse year is allowed to drift from the 2020 base, which is exactly the failure mode behind our label-circularity concern, and the cheapest experiment surfaced in this loop after FDA.
